checklist.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Does recover_polynomialcoeff correctly truncate recovered polynomial to degree < FIELD_ELEMENTS_PER_BLOB?

reachability.notes: If an attacker provides mutually inconsistent cells, the recovered polynomial may have non-zero high-degree coefficients. Missing truncation or missing validation of high-degree zeroes could produce a polynomial outside the original blob domain.

checklist.test_procedure: 1. Identify the recover_polynomialcoeff function implementation (SG-023). 2. Verify that the function returns only poly_coeff[:FIELD_ELEMENTS_PER_BLOB] and not the full extended domain. 3. Craft test cases with mutually inconsistent cell inputs that could produce non-zero high-degree coefficients in the extension domain. 4. Verify that coefficients at indices >= FIELD_ELEMENTS_PER_BLOB are explicitly validated to be zero OR are truncated before use. 5. Check that any polynomial returned from recovery cannot have degree >= FIELD_ELEMENTS_PER_BLOB. 6. Test that cells/proofs generated from a recovered polynomial with truncated high-degree terms match the original commitment.
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-0035, Invariant: SG-023-INV-003, Trust Boundary: tb-009. CRITICAL: If high-degree coefficients are nonzero after recovery, the truncated polynomial differs from the original. Cells and proofs generated from this incorrect polynomial would not match the original commitment, causing silent data corruption. Bug bounty eligible - requires demonstrating inconsistent cell inputs that produce nonzero high-degree coefficients after recovery.

checklist.title: Verify Recovery Engine handles inconsistent cell inputs safely

reachability.notes: If an attacker provides mutually inconsistent cells, the recovered polynomial may have non-zero high-degree coefficients. Missing truncation or missing validation of high-degree zeroes could produce a polynomial outside the original blob domain.

checklist.test_procedure: 1. Trace the data flow from P2P layer to recover_polynomialcoeff. 2. Identify what validation exists on incoming cells before polynomial recovery. 3. Create test vectors with cells that are mutually inconsistent (i.e., cannot be derived from any valid degree < FIELD_ELEMENTS_PER_BLOB polynomial). 4. Execute recovery with inconsistent inputs and examine the output polynomial. 5. Verify the system either: (a) detects inconsistency and rejects the input, OR (b) validates that high-degree coefficients are zero after recovery, OR (c) correctly truncates and does not rely on invalid data. 6. Check for absence of silent corruption where invalid recovery produces different data than original blob.
checklist.notes: Supporting boundary check for actor-recovery-engine. Attacker-controlled data from P2P network crosses trust boundary at tb-009. The recovery engine must not trust that cells are consistent.

checklist.title: Verify Proof Generator receives only valid-domain polynomials

reachability.notes: If an attacker provides mutually inconsistent cells, the recovered polynomial may have non-zero high-degree coefficients. Missing truncation or missing validation of high-degree zeroes could produce a polynomial outside the original blob domain.

checklist.test_procedure: 1. Identify the interface between recovery engine and proof generator. 2. Verify that polynomials passed to proof generation are guaranteed to have degree < FIELD_ELEMENTS_PER_BLOB. 3. Check if proof generator has independent validation of polynomial degree. 4. Test that proofs generated from a correctly recovered (truncated) polynomial match the original blob's commitment. 5. Verify that if an attacker could somehow inject a higher-degree polynomial, the proof generator would either reject it or produce proofs that fail verification.
checklist.notes: Supporting node check for actor-proof-generator. Downstream of recovery, ensures proof generation receives correctly-bounded polynomials.
